text:
Travis Konecny needed 17 seconds to put Philadelphia ahead in Washington. It was the last time all night the Flyers looked like the team that had won three straight. The Capitals, winless in five (0-5-0) coming in, took the game over from there and turned it into a 7-3 rout at Capital One Arena.

Ryan Leonard answered three minutes later with a backhand, the kind of goal that comes from a player whose confidence is running high: he had a four-game goal streak earlier this month and put five shots on goal here. The game tilted in the second period. Washington out-chanced Philadelphia 1.74 to 0.99 in expected goals (the quality of the chances each side created), Cole Hutson scored on the power play after a Porter Martone penalty, and Boone Jenner made it 3-1 on a 3% chance after Joseph Woll got caught playing the puck. "Caps ran them out of the building," PHLY Sports' Charlie O'Connor posted after 40 minutes, and the numbers agree. Hutson's goal was the biggest swing of the night, moving Washington from 54% to 75% to win.

Rasmus Ristolainen pulled the Flyers within one early in the third, but they never really pushed. Alex Tuch tipped one in at 17:01, Matt Roy and Ivan Miroshnichenko followed inside two minutes, and Dylan Strome added one with 11 seconds left after Cole Knuble's late goal. Tuch finished with a goal and two assists in 21:54. By shot quality, Washington deserved to win this about 70% of the time, so the score flatters the margin more than the result.

Woll had a rough one: six goals on 34 shots, about 2.5 more than those shots deserved. For a Flyers team living with trade talk around Konecny, who also had an assist here, and endless questions about Matvei Michkov, this was a night to forget quickly. For the Capitals, in what has been billed as Alex Ovechkin's final season, it was a reminder that the losing streak was not the whole picture. They had beaten Philadelphia 5-2 in October, too.
headline: Capitals end the skid by running the Flyers out
